head: fd2132353430d9885b34ef9872d76d7118c41603
summary:
Fail. The issue's outcome is still not delivered.

What is done correctly: the guarded close path checks that the PR actually merged into the default branch (head, base, parent and ancestry), and it allows exactly one Closes #N reference. Before writing, it re-checks the issue contract, labels, assignees, the timeline digest and the guard owner. It never takes over a later claim, and any unknown result keeps the guard and leaves the issue open. Existing CI, performance, review, protected-branch, no-bypass and return-to-todo gates are unchanged. No schedule is deployed.

What this head adds: a check that releases the guard only after refusals that are known to happen before any write. This repair is correct. It covers pending CI, a stale review and contract changes, and a two-wake control tests it.

What still blocks:
- recovery_entry.verify_rollout always refuses. Every guarded writer, the adoption publisher and the recovery wake stop before any issue write, so after an asynchronous merge the linked issue still stays open.
- A queued guarded PR keeps its guard. The next wake cannot take that guard, so it calls block_unadmitted, which posts a pending status over the queued PR's success. Nothing restores the success status, so the queued merge is blocked permanently.
- No hosted asynchronous merge has closed its issue automatically. The Core #77 fixture records a manual close.
- The controlled hosted comparison of the issues:write permission hypothesis is absent.
- Adoption by all actors and launchers, request ownership and safe cancellation remain unproven.

findings.title: Verified post-merge closure remains unreachable
findings.detail: verify_rollout always raises. The guarded writer, the adoption guard, target-review preflight and recovery main all stop before any issue write, so linked issues stay open after an asynchronous merge.
findings.required_fix: Implement and review a rollout-evidence verifier. Deploy recovery through reviewed policy adoption. Then demonstrate an automatic close.

findings.title: Later wakes permanently block a queued guarded PR
findings.detail: After enqueue reports 'queued', the writer keeps the merge guard (settle and the reconcile post-loop return 'retained'). On the next wake, guarded.begin fails with merge_guard_held_or_consumed, and reconcile then calls block_unadmitted. That posts a pending claude/verified-merge status over the queued PR's success status. No path restores success, so GitHub's native merge never completes.
findings.required_fix: Tie the queued request and success status to the guard owner, and skip re-blocking a PR whose authenticated owner still holds a live queued request. Alternatively, implement a safe path to take over or re-verify it. Add consecutive-wake controls for a queued PR.

findings.title: No hosted asynchronous merge, automatic-close proof or permission comparison
findings.detail: All controls are synthetic. The Core #77 fixture records a manual close. The controlled hosted test of the issues:write hypothesis is absent.
findings.required_fix: Run hosted positive and negative asynchronous merge controls that close the linked issue, plus the controlled issues:write comparison.

findings.title: Actor/launcher adoption and request ownership unproven
findings.detail: actor_rollout is always 'unknown'. guarded_admission.cancel_blocked keeps every request because the shared Actions bot identity cannot prove which run created it, and cancellation is not implemented.
findings.required_fix: Provide verified actor and launcher adoption evidence and request provenance bound to the exact policy and runtime, with controls.
